daily_reality.summary: Medical records specialists (health information technicians) organize, manage, and code patient health data. They work in hospitals, physician offices, insurance companies, and government agencies. Primarily computer-based work ensuring accuracy, completeness, and security of medical records.
typical_tasks: Reviewing patient records for accuracy and completeness
Assigning diagnostic and procedure codes (ICD-10-CM, CPT, HCPCS)
Ensuring HIPAA compliance for all records handling
Auditing medical records for coding accuracy and compliance
Abstracting clinical data for registries and reporting
Resolving coding discrepancies with clinical staff
Generating reports on coding, quality, and compliance metrics
key_documents: Patient medical records and discharge summaries

deadlines.cms_reporting: Quarterly and annual deadlines for quality measures
deadlines.credential_renewal: Varies: RHIT every 2 years with 20 CE credits

daily_reality.seasonality: Year-end coding pushes for fiscal year reporting. ICD-10 annual updates (October 1). Open enrollment periods create insurance-related volume.

regulatory.summary: HIPAA is the foundational privacy and security law. AHIMA credentials (RHIT, RHIA, CCS) are industry standards. ICD-10-CM/PCS coding follows CMS guidelines. Growing regulatory complexity with value-based care and quality reporting requirements.

key_laws.name: HIPAA (Health Insurance Portability and Accountability Act)
key_laws.description: Federal law governing patient health information privacy and security

key_laws.name: HITECH Act
key_laws.description: Strengthened HIPAA enforcement and promoted EHR adoption

key_laws.name: State health information laws
key_laws.description: State-specific regulations on medical records retention, release, and privacy

requirements: Associate's degree minimum from CAHIIM-accredited program (RHIT pathway)
Pass AHIMA certification exam (RHIT, RHIA, CCS, CCA)
20 CE credits every 2 years for RHIT renewal
No state licensure required in most states

regulatory.recent_changes: Annual ICD-10-CM updates (October 1, 2025). Growing use of computer-assisted coding (CAC) and AI in coding workflows. Value-based care models increasing data quality demands. CMS expanding quality reporting requirements.

tools.summary: EHR systems, coding software with encoder/grouper tools, HIPAA compliance platforms, and increasingly AI-powered computer-assisted coding (CAC).

primary_tools.name: EHR systems
primary_tools.description: Electronic health record platforms where medical data is stored and managed

primary_tools.name: Coding encoder/grouper software
primary_tools.description: Tools for assigning ICD-10, CPT, and HCPCS codes

primary_tools.name: Computer-Assisted Coding (CAC) software
primary_tools.description: AI-powered tools suggesting codes from clinical documentation

primary_tools.name: Release of Information (ROI) systems
primary_tools.description: Platforms for managing patient record release requests

primary_tools.name: CDI (Clinical Documentation Improvement) software
primary_tools.description: Tools for improving clinical documentation quality

secondary_tools: Reference tools: ICD-10 codebooks, CPT manuals, AHA Coding Clinic
pain_points: Constant regulatory and coding guideline changes
EHR system complexity and interoperability issues
High volume of records with tight turnaround deadlines
Physician documentation quality affecting coding accuracy
Concerns about AI/CAC replacing manual coding roles

terminology.summary: Health information management terminology combining medical coding, privacy/security, and healthcare administration vocabulary.

terms.RHIA: Registered Health Information Administrator (higher AHIMA credential)
terms.ICD-10-CM: International Classification of Diseases, 10th Revision, Clinical Modification — diagnosis codes
terms.ICD-10-PCS: ICD-10 Procedure Coding System — inpatient procedure codes
terms.CPT: Current Procedural Terminology — outpatient procedure/service codes
terms.HCPCS: Healthcare Common Procedure Coding System — Medicare/Medicaid codes
terms.HIPAA: Health Insurance Portability and Accountability Act — privacy law
terms.PHI: Protected Health Information — patient data covered by HIPAA
terms.ROI: Release of Information — authorized disclosure of medical records
terms.CDI: Clinical Documentation Improvement — enhancing physician documentation for coding
terms.CAC: Computer-Assisted Coding — AI-suggested coding from documentation
terms.EHR/EMR: Electronic Health Record / Electronic Medical Record
terms.abstracting: Extracting and summarizing key data from medical records
terms.encoder: Software tool that assists with code assignment
terms.compliance: Adherence to coding guidelines, HIPAA, and billing regulations

career_psychology.summary: Fast-growing field (15% projected growth) with strong remote work potential. Median salary varies widely: $45K-$75K for RHIT, higher with coding specialization (CCS: $75K+). AI is changing but not eliminating coding roles. Strong demand for certified professionals.
career_path: Associate's degree in health information technology (CAHIIM-accredited)
Pass AHIMA exam → earn RHIT or CCA credential
Entry-level medical records specialist or coding technician
Senior coder, coding auditor, or CDI specialist
fears: Coding errors leading to compliance audits and fines
Rapid regulatory changes making skills obsolete
motivation: Detail-oriented work with clear quality metrics
Critical role in healthcare revenue cycle

community.summary: AHIMA is the primary professional organization. Active coding forums and communities online. AAPC provides alternative certification pathway.

associations.name: American Health Information Management Association (AHIMA)
associations.type: Primary professional organization for HIM professionals

associations.name: AAPC (formerly American Academy of Professional Coders)
associations.type: Professional organization for medical coders (CPC, CRC credentials)

associations.name: CAHIIM (Commission on Accreditation for Health Informatics and Information Management Education)
associations.type: Accrediting body for HIM educational programs

online_communities.name: r/CodingandBilling
online_communities.description: Reddit community for medical coding and billing

market.summary: Fastest-growing HIM field: 15% growth projected 2024-2034. ~3,200 annual openings. Remote coding positions expanding. AI/CAC changing but not eliminating roles — shifting to oversight and quality assurance. Value-based care increasing data quality demands.

demand_forecast.driver: EHR adoption, value-based care, regulatory complexity

market_trends: 15% growth rate — one of the fastest in healthcare
AI/CAC augmenting but not replacing certified coders
Remote work becoming standard for coding positions
Value-based care increasing data quality demands
Annual ICD-10 updates requiring continuous learning
CDI roles expanding as documentation quality becomes critical
Healthcare data analytics creating new career pathways
